LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 5.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY:

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.1: Listening and Speaking 5.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary:
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 5.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary:, part of Strand 5 in Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why should we listen carefully? 2. How can we improve our pronunciatio n?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. listen actively to a variety of texts to gain information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 5.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. apply vocabulary related to the theme in a variety of contexts for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 5.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. use the language pattern correctly for effective oral communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 5.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. promote listening to a variety of texts for information and enjoyment.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 5.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. promote listening to a variety of texts for information and enjoyment.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to audio-visual recordings of songs, stories and passages featuring the sounds /ʊ/ /uː/ /æ/ /f/ /v/,

2. respond to questions from the listening text,

3. construct sentences related to a story or listening comprehension using the language pattern, (noun phrase + would like to be ...),

4. retell a story he or she has listened to accurately,

5. respond correctly to questions based on the text, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to audio-visual recordings of songs, stories and passages featuring the sounds /ʊ/ /uː/ /æ/ /f/ /v/,
2. respond to questions from the listening text,
3. construct sentences related to a story or listening comprehension using the language pattern, (noun phrase + would like to be ...),
4. retell a story he or she has listened to accurately,
5. respond correctly to questions based on the text, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 5.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner participates in sharing their thoughts as they discuss

collaboratively.

• Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: This is cultivated as the learner is able to draw conclusions from the listening

text.

Values:
Love: This is cultivated as the learner is able to portray a caring attitude to special groups of people that require meals with

diverse nutritional value.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Prevention of lifestyle or non-communicable diseases: This is promoted as the learner is informed on a balanced diet for

varied nutritional needs.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the theme of nutrition to their learning in Agriculture.
